title: Rehearsing at Nola Studio and first USO dates
summary: They build a 59-minute show at Nola Studio, play for troops in Pennsylvania and New England, and are offered a trip to Asia.

story.theme_name: Drafted: musicians in the military and the war years
story.community_name: Drafted: service bands, USO shows and the war years

blocks.x: They had a big room for us to rehearse the band, rehearsed and he brought in some show people, some acts, and we rehearsed and then he had us to play some band tunes, which we did. So we put together a show that lasted in there in about 59 minutes. And we hung around there about a week, rehearsing, doing nothing. Then our first date was -- they put us on a train, sent us out to Clarendon, Pennsylvania. We played there for the troops, and this was immediately after the war, see. The war had just -- the Armistice had just been signed, see. And so the barracks

were just going through a period of some of the troops being discharged and whatnot. We left there and went to New England, played all through New England. Came on back down to Providence, Rhode Island. He called me up that night, he said, "Phillars, how would you like to go to Asia? We'll send you to Japan. Do you think you want to go?" I said, "Yes!"

He said, "I'll tell you what I'm going to do. I'm going to bring your whole outfit in tomorrow and we'll start rehearsing, and we'll start processing you. You'll get passports and things like that." This we did. We came on in. He said, "While you're in town, all you have to do is have everybody call at my office about 12:00 every day. I may want you to go down to the Battery and play for some troops that come in, which would be maybe about an hour's work, and then I want you to go here and do this." And said, "It's nothing certain about it, but just keep in touch with us." And we were down there three weeks before we did anything. All we had to do was call in, see.
